articles.title: Fantasy Booking a WWE Survivor Series Match Between Every Era's Best Team
articles.summary: What if every era in WWE history assembled its five defining Superstars for one massive, six-team Survivor Series elimination match?
articles.body:
What if every era in WWE history assembled its five defining Superstars for one massive, six-team Survivor Series elimination match?

Yes, it would be chaotic and almost too much for one ring to contain, but it also creates a fun "what if" scenario for fans to debate.

Could Hulk Hogan captain a team from the Golden Era to victory, despite the enemies he made during his career? Could Shawn Michaels and Bret Hart coexist long enough? Is the Ruthless Aggression unit the most impressive of the bunch?

Find out who makes the cut—and which team survives a five-on-five-on-five-on-five-on-five-on-five showdown—in this fantasy booking exercise.

Superstars: Hulk Hogan (captain), "Macho Man" Randy Savage, Andre the Giant, "The Million Dollar Man" Ted DiBiase and The Ultimate Warrior

Five larger-than-life icons come together to represent the Golden Era of WWE, with Hulk Hogan captaining the squad.

A highly decorated bunch, with four of the five members holding a world championship at least once, this collection of stars looks unbeatable on paper. Even more so when you realize that Hogan held the WWE Championship for four years during his first reign and only lost it due to chicanery on the part of Andre and DiBiase.

And therein lies the issues facing the 1980s unit: Hogan has had notable, high-profile issues with all four of his partners, perhaps none more memorable or intense than the disintegration of his Mega Powers friendship with Savage.

The rich, not-always-pleasant history between the captain and his teammates would be cause for concern and perhaps the undoing of the entire team in a battle for era supremacy.

Superstars: Bret Hart (captain), Shawn Michaels, Diesel, Razor Ramon and The Undertaker

The New Generation is often forgotten, the abyss of WWE creativity lodged between the Golden and Attitude Eras. It is where bad gimmicks like Bastion Booger, Mantaur and Dr. Isaac Yankem DDS roamed, and Vince McMahon lost track of what the audience wanted from their professional wrestling product.

With that said, it also produced some of the biggest, best and most beloved wrestlers ever, led by Bret Hart and Shawn Michaels.

Respected by generations of talent after them for their excellence between the ropes, no other team would be able to boast two better competitors than they do at the one and two spots. When you add The Undertaker, perhaps the most respected Superstar in WWE history, the team is that much more impressive.

The universally cool guys Diesel and Ramon round out the lineup, making this one, arguably, the most impressive on paper.

Where the New Generation would struggle is with egos.

Hart and Michaels have the most documented personal beef in pro wrestling history, while the latter's real-life best friends, Diesel and Ramon, would likely only throw gasoline on the fire.

With Undertaker likely to chokeslam all of them and walk out on the nonsense, what might be the best team on paper could also be the most combustible.

Superstars: "Stone Cold" Steve Austin (captain), The Rock, Mankind, Kane and Triple H

Can "Stone Cold" Steve Austin and The Rock, two generational icons whose competitive sides are well documented, coexist long enough to lead the Attitude Era team to victory?

Probably. Neither Superstar likes anything more than emerging victorious from a high-profile matchup. They are both uber-competitive, and while they have had their differences, they have also teamed up to win main event tag matches.

The question is whether they could coexist with their teammates.

Kane and Mankind had their battles, but were also tag team champions. Triple H, leader of multiple factions over the course of his career, understands teamwork and what it takes to put personal issues aside in the name of a win.

While there were intense rivalries between all five guys on this team, including the time Triple H masterminded a hit-and-run attack on Stone Cold, there is enough reason to believe that the egos here could coexist just long enough to stick it to the opposition and eke out a win.

As long as Triple H doesn't taunt Kane with any mentions of Katie Vick.

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

Superstars: John Cena (captain), Brock Lesnar, Randy Orton, Batista and Edge

The Ruthless Aggression team is stacked with megastars and world champions, four of whom trained together at Ohio Valley Wrestling before making the jump to WWE's main roster and becoming defining stars of the era.

Cena, a record 17-time world champion, would be the logical captain, but could Lesnar and Orton—two of his most memorable rivals—take orders from him?

Add to that dynamic Batista, who ultimately stepped out on his own when he no longer believed in the vision Triple H had for Evolution, and you have a potential wild card at play.

The Rated-R Superstar is already one of the most untrustworthy villains in WWE history. Whether he will do what is best for the team or for himself is something to watch.

If all five could stay united, though, this would be the most unstoppable team of the bunch.

Superstars: Roman Reigns, Seth Rollins, Dean Ambrose, Daniel Bryan and AJ Styles

Sierra. Hotel. India. Echo. Lima. Delta.

Since The Shield's debut in 2012, Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins have dominated WWE, winning world titles, headlining WrestleManias and captivating fans around the globe through unforgettable matches and some of the most layered storytelling in company history.

Add former partner Dean Ambrose to the mix, and you have the reunited Shield, one of the most dominant trios to grace a pro wrestling ring. Sure, Rollins has a history of untrustworthiness, but for the most part, when they have been united, no one can stop them.

Daniel Bryan had some success against The Shield, but he was among the group's first targets. He has battled all three men with varying degrees of success, but he is also a professional wrestler whose main goal is to win.

Ditto AJ Styles, who can let his temper get the best of him but could keep it in check to get a W.

How Bryan and Styles coexist with the other three would decide the fate of the PG Era team.

Superstars: Cody Rhodes (captain...or is he?), Drew McIntyre, CM Punk (captain?), Kevin Owens and Sami Zayn

The biggest issue facing the Current Era team is chemistry: CM Punk and Cody Rhodes get along, but the rest of the group may struggle to put personal differences aside.

Even within that group of haters, there is a rich history of distrust and destruction—much of it rooted in Kevin Owens and Sami Zayn's on-again, off-again friendship.

Add in Drew McIntyre, who seemingly dislikes everyone and has had heated rivalries with both Rhodes and Punk, and you have a combustible team.

At the same time, Owens and Zayn defeated arguably the best tag team in WWE history, The Usos, in the main event of WrestleMania 39's first night—proof that they can put their differences aside and succeed together.

This team's success may depend on whether its members can put their egos aside—and whether Punk, McIntyre, Owens and Zayn can avoid mouthing off to one another and disrupting the team's cohesion.

Winners: PG Era (Reigns, Rollins, Ambrose survive)

So successful was The Shield at the height of their dominance that they could overcome anything and anyone. This is a trio that was thrown into the fire and dominated altercations with John Cena, The Rock, Daniel Bryan, Kane, The Big Show, Brock Lesnar, etc.

Even if Bryan and Styles do not coexist with them, or are eliminated early, the trio is more than capable of staying focused on the end game, triple powerbombing an industry icon like Hogan, Austin, Hart, or Michaels through a table, and picking up the ultimate Survivor Series win.

Their only roadblock could be CM Punk, who not only introduced them to the WWE Universe at the 2012 Survivor Series event, but also inexplicably beat them in a 3-on-1 Handicap Match at the 2013 TLC event.

If The Best in the World is left standing for his team and confronted with knocking off The Shield, it is not necessarily an impossible feat.

Still, despite all of the defining Superstars involved in this prospective match, there is no threesome more united at their strongest than The Shield, as evidenced by the emotional moment shared by Rollins and Reigns recently at the end of the SummerSlam premium live event, where they paid homage to the group that started their journey to the Hall of Fame.

What may have been the weakest of the teams on paper earns the victory, thanks to their proven history as a unit and their success against stars far bigger than them.

articles.title: Czech Republic Bars Russia's Team From Under-18 Women's Ice Hockey Worlds
articles.summary: PRAGUE (AP) — The Czech Republic will not allow Russia's team to compete at the under-18 women's ice hockey world championship in January, the government's interior minister said on Wednesday.
articles.body:
PRAGUE (AP) — The Czech Republic will not allow Russia's team to compete at the under-18 women's ice hockey world championship in January, the government's interior minister said on Wednesday.

"There are government regulations, a government resolution, in place that, de facto, prohibit the issuance of visas for Russian athletes to participate in our championship," Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said after meeting the representatives of the Czech Ice Hockey Federation.

The minister referred to a government directive from 2023 that banned Russian athletes from receiving Czech visas due to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine a year earlier.

Metnar said another government member, Foreign Minister Petr Macinka, had informed the other countries in the European visa-free Schengen zone about the Czech stance.

Even if the Russians are granted visas in another Schengen zone country, his ministry "has legal tools to solve such a situation," Metnar said. "Entry into Czech territory would not be permitted."

The Czechs will inform the International Ice Hockey Federation about their position, secretary general Jan Černý said.

"For us, it is crucial to able to host the championship here and that it is safe," Černý said.

The eight-team tournament is scheduled for January 8–16 in the city of Ostrava.

The Czech announcement follows a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling late last month. It overturned an IIHF ban on Russian national teams that had been in place since soon after the invasion of Ukraine.

The CAS ruling has prompted a backlash in hockey. Seven European nations at the 16-team men's world championship scheduled in May have said they will not play against Russia in the tournament. Germany, too, is weighing up whether it can continue as host.

The IIHF is also facing pressure from sponsors who don't want their brands associated with the Russian team.

Russia won't compete at the world junior hockey championship starting next month because of tournament host Canada's decision to bar its players.

The governments of Finland, Sweden and Norway have all either tightened their border controls to bar entry to Russian athletes, or have said they are planning to.

articles.title: Selene Melián desvela por qué Nico Paz decidió no regresar al Real Madrid: "Conozco a su familia y sé de lo que hablo"

articles.summary: La contertulia de La Tribu defendió que fue el propio futbolista quien decidió continuar en el Como y su apuesta por jugar con Argentina
articles.body: El futuro de Nico Paz en el Real Madrid sigue siendo uno de los temas de conversación más atractivos tras su gran partido con Argentina. Selene Melián, periodista de Radio MARCA Tenerife, aportó información de primera mano sobre la decisión del internacional argentino de continuar en el Como, asegurando que fue el propio futbolista quien prefirió permanecer en Italia antes que regresar al Santiago Bernabéu para asumir un papel secundario. "La información que manejamos aquí en Radio MARCA y a nivel particular es que Nico Paz ha sido el que ha decidido quedarse este año en el Como", explicó Melián, destacando la importancia de Cesc Fàbregas en el crecimiento del centrocampista. Según la periodista, el jugador tenía garantizado un protagonismo que difícilmente habría encontrado en el Real Madrid debido a la competencia existente en su posición. La contertulia insistió en que su información procede de la cercanía con el entorno familiar del futbolista, cuyo padre, Pablo Paz, fue internacional con Argentina y jugó en el Tenerife. "Conozco a Nico Paz y a su familia y sé de lo que hablo", respondió durante un intercambio de opiniones especialmente tenso. Melián también quiso aclarar otro de los asuntos que han acompañado la trayectoria del futbolista: su elección de representar a Argentina en lugar de España. La periodista recordó una entrevista concedida por Pablo Paz a Radio MARCA Tenerife cuando Javier Mascherano convocó por primera vez a su hijo para la selección Argentina sub-20. Según explicó, el padre del jugador aseguró entonces que la Real Federación Española de Fútbol nunca se había puesto en contacto con Nico Paz. Por tanto, el centrocampista no tuvo que elegir entre dos propuestas internacionales. "La Federación nunca se había puesto en contacto con Nico Paz, por eso Nico nunca tuvo que elegir si jugar con España o jugar con Argentina", recordó Melián, que también destacó la ilusión del futbolista por compartir vestuario con Leo Messi y defender la camiseta que había representado su padre. La periodista cerró su argumentación poniendo sobre la mesa la enorme competencia que existe en el centro del campo madridista: "¿A quién quitas en el Real Madrid a día de hoy para poner a Nico Paz de forma indiscutible? ¿A Bellingham lo quitas?". "Por supuesto que Nico Paz un día quiere jugar en el Real Madrid, pero este año tenía la garantía absoluta de jugarlo todo con Cesc Fàbregas", explicó.

articles.title: Tayfun Korkut explica las claves de la explosión de Arda Güler: "La mejora física ha sido la clave de todo"

articles.summary: El exfutbolista y entrenador turco analizó la evolución de su compatriota tras su renovación hasta 2032 y defendió la gestión de Carlo Ancelotti
articles.body: La renovación de Arda Güler con el Real Madrid hasta 2032 ha sido una de las grandes noticias de la jornada. El internacional turco ha ampliado su compromiso con el conjunto blanco después de consolidarse como una pieza importante del equipo y de firmar grandes actuaciones con su selección. Una progresión que Tayfun Korkut, exfutbolista y entrenador turco, ha analizado en Directo MARCA, donde ha señalado el aspecto físico como el principal responsable de su crecimiento. "La evolución ha sido buena en los últimos años y creo que es un buen momento para el club y también para él", explicó Korkut, que ha seguido de cerca la trayectoria de su compatriota desde sus primeros pasos en el fútbol turco. Uno de los asuntos que abordó Korkut fue la falta de protagonismo de Arda Güler durante sus primeras temporadas en el Real Madrid. Lejos de criticar a Carlo Ancelotti, el técnico defendió la gestión del italiano y aseguró que aquella etapa resultó fundamental para la evolución del centrocampista. "Yo no creo que Ancelotti dudara de su talento, pero no estaba todavía físicamente preparado. Creo que le protegió", afirmó. Korkut, que pudo ver al jugador en directo durante su etapa en Turquía y también recientemente con su selección, destacó el cambio que ha experimentado desde su llegada al Santiago Bernabéu. "En el Real Madrid no es solo tocar el balón, también hay que correr. Se pide intensidad, hay muchas transiciones y todo eso fue un proceso", explicó el exentrenador, convencido de que el futbolista ha trabajado especialmente para adaptarse a esas exigencias. "La mejora física fue la clave de todo eso, porque confianza él tiene, a veces demasiada", añadió. Más allá de su evolución física, Korkut quiso destacar la personalidad del internacional turco, que ya asumía una enorme responsabilidad durante su etapa en el Fenerbahçe. "De una cosa nunca he dudado, de su responsabilidad y de su mentalidad", aseguró, recordando que jugar en el conjunto de Estambul también implica soportar una gran presión. El entrenador explicó que esa experiencia le ayudó a prepararse mentalmente para dar el salto al Real Madrid, aunque necesitaba tiempo para alcanzar el nivel físico exigido por la élite. Korkut también defendió la paciencia que tuvo Ancelotti con el jugador cuando llegó con apenas 18 años, pese a las críticas que recibió en Turquía por su escasa participación. "Los primeros pasos con Ancelotti también fueron importantes para él, aunque le costó y no a todo el mundo le gustó", señaló. Para el exfutbolista turco, la renovación hasta 2032 supone el reconocimiento a un proceso de adaptación que ha permitido a Arda Güler transformar su talento en rendimiento. Y considera que todavía tiene margen para seguir creciendo: "Tiene cosas que puede mejorar y va a mejorar seguramente, porque está en uno de los mejores equipos del mundo".

articles.title: NHL 2027 Winter Classic Jerseys for Avalanche, Mammoth Revealed in Videos, Photos
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche and Utah Mammoth are embracing new looks for their New Year's Eve outdoor matchup.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche and Utah Mammoth are embracing new looks for their New Year's Eve outdoor matchup.

The Avs and Mammoth revealed a first look Wednesday at specialty jerseys for the 2027 NHL Winter Classic.

The NHL is set to drop the puck at Rice-Eccles Stadium Salt Lake City Dec. 31 at 6 p.m. ET.

According to the NHL, the lettering on the Avalanche jersey is "inspired by signage found throughout mountain towns of the Colorado Rocky Mountains in the 19th century and the railway lines that connected them to Denver."

The helmets, which mark the first burgundy editions in franchise history, feature a Colorado flag "inspired by the old patches found on hockey coaches' cardigans," according to the NHL.

The Mammoth's helmet features stripes and lettering inspired by Utah's first ice skating facility, Hygeia Iceland, according to the team, as well as an interior collar designed to mimic vintage ski sweaters.

The upcoming Winter Classic will mark the first outdoor game for the Mammoth, which arrived in Salt Lake City in 2024 after relocating from Arizona.

The Avalanche have previously hosted three outdoor games, most recently playing as the home team in a 2021 contest against the Vegas Golden Knights at Lake Tahoe. This will mark the Avs' first outdoor contest as a visitor.

The new editions to the Mammoth and Avalanche uniform lineups comes two weeks after all 32 NHL team revealed new Hometown Remix uniforms.

The jersey reveal also took place before the Mammoth and Avalanche meet for a Winter Classic preview Wednesday night at Delta Center. The Mammoth are looking to snap out of an 0-3-3 slump against an Avs roster missing both Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar when the puck drops at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: In 2026,WNBA generated $608 million in sponsor value, with Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever driving $205 million, over one-third of broadcast returns, despite playing in just 13% of games, while Atlanta Dream powered major team-level deals
articles.summary: In 2026, the WNBA achieved a remarkable $608 million in sponsor media value, driven significantly by Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever's national exposure, highlighting the league's growth and team partnerships.
articles.body: The WNBA generated an estimated $608 million in sponsor media value during the 2026 regular season, a 53.9 per cent increase on the previous year, according to a new report from Relo Metrics. The figures reveal how much national television exposure, the league’s expanding broadcast partnerships and the popularity of Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are contributing to the commercial value of women’s basketball. But the findings also show that brands do not necessarily need a league-wide agreement to benefit, with several team-level partnerships producing substantial returns.WNBA sponsorship value rises to $608 million as broadcast exposure drives growthThe WNBA generated $608 million in Sponsor Media Value (SMV) during the 2026 regular season, up 53.9 per cent year on year, according to the 2026 WNBA Regular Season Sponsorship Report released by Relo Metrics on November 12. The figure measures the estimated value of brand exposure across broadcasts and social media, rather than the amount of money paid to the league through sponsorship contracts.Broadcast exposure accounted for more than $545 million, approximately 90 per cent of the total, while social media contributed nearly $63 million. Broadcast media value increased by 62 per cent compared with the previous season, making television and other broadcast coverage the principal source of the league’s sponsorship value.The increase coincided with the first year of the WNBA’s new 11-year media rights agreement, which brought NBC, NBC Sports and USA Network into the league’s broadcast portfolio. Those new partners contributed $105 million in Sponsor Media Value, according to Relo Metrics. That represents roughly 19 per cent of the $545 million generated through broadcast exposure.The report also found that the value was concentrated among a relatively small group of major partners. Michelob Ultra, Nike, State Farm, Coinbase and Tampax collectively generated nearly $247 million in Sponsor Media Value, accounting for approximately 41 per cent of the league-wide total. Their combined figure illustrates the commercial advantage available to brands with prominent league-level agreements, although the findings also identify opportunities for companies working directly with individual teams.Relo Metrics is an artificial intelligence-powered sports sponsorship intelligence platform and a division of GumGum, a technology company specialising in advertising and contextual intelligence. Its platform measures brand exposure across live sports broadcasts, social media and streaming, helping sponsors, teams and leagues assess the visibility and estimated media value of their partnerships.“The WNBA offers several ways for brands to reach basketball fans,” said Ryan Meizinger, Director of Insights and Strategic Services at Relo Metrics. “While league partnerships remain the strongest guarantee to capitalize on women’s basketball, it is a team’s schedule and the placement of a logo that shapes the value of the partnership. Good team deals can put brands in front of national audiences.”Caitlin Clark and Indiana Fever account for more than a third of broadcast valueThe Indiana Fever were one of the clearest examples of how a team’s national profile can influence the commercial value of the league. The franchise generated $205 million in broadcast Sponsor Media Value, accounting for approximately 37.6 per cent of the WNBA’s $545 million broadcast total.The figure is particularly notable because the Fever played in only 13 per cent of the league’s regular-season games. They were also the only team whose every game was shown nationally, giving sponsors attached to the franchise repeated access to a much wider television audience than teams without the same level of coverage.Caitlin Clark’s profile has been central to the Fever’s visibility, with her performances and the attention surrounding the team helping attract viewers across the season. The report also found that Clark and the Fever dominated social media value, although the commercial growth was not limited to Indianapolis.The other 14 teams collectively generated $48 million in full media value through their social media posts, alongside 101 million engagements. That figure points to the value of team-owned content outside live broadcasts, including player photographs, video clips, behind-the-scenes material, Instagram reels and question-and-answer sessions that give supporters more direct access to players.Uniforms were particularly effective in extending sponsorship exposure onto social platforms. They generated more than $40 million in social media value, with social accounting for 39 per cent of the uniforms’ total value. In practical terms, a sponsor’s logo could continue appearing in player photographs and video content long after a game had ended, adding another source of visibility beyond television coverage.Across all sponsorship assets, the floor court logo, baseline apron signage and uniforms were the three most valuable placements. Together, they generated 53 per cent of the WNBA’s total Sponsor Media Value. The findings indicate that where a brand appears can be as important as the size of its partnership, particularly when an asset is repeatedly visible during nationally televised games or reproduced through social media content.The report also identified a relationship between team performance and sponsorship exposure. Seven of the eight teams leading the SMV rankings had winning records during the season. Relo Metrics suggested that successful teams could be better positioned to secure more national primetime appearances in 2027, creating further opportunities for their commercial partners.Albert shows how brands can benefit without a league-wide dealAlthough the five leading league sponsors accounted for approximately 41 per cent of the total value, Relo Metrics found that brands could generate substantial exposure through agreements with individual franchises. Around 85 brands recorded at least $1 million in Sponsor Media Value during the season, demonstrating that the commercial opportunities extended well beyond the league’s biggest partnerships.Financial services and healthcare were two particularly competitive categories. Together, they generated $123 million, or approximately 20 per cent of the WNBA’s total Sponsor Media Value. A combined 23 brands in those sectors crossed the $1 million mark, comprising 11 in financial services and 12 in healthcare. Unlike categories such as beer and apparel, where one dominant partner had a stronger position, neither financial services nor healthcare was controlled by a single brand.The report highlighted Albert, a personal finance and fintech company, as an example of how a business can establish a significant presence through team partnerships. Albert served as the official jersey-patch partner of the Atlanta Dream, Dallas Wings and Los Angeles Sparks, with its branding appearing in 87 nationally televised games.The company generated $14.7 million in Sponsor Media Value, placing it 10th among more than 400 brands analysed by Relo Metrics, despite not having a league-wide sponsorship agreement. Its ranking illustrates how a carefully selected group of team partnerships can deliver national exposure without the cost or scale of a central league deal.The findings arrive as the WNBA continues to expand its footprint. The league currently has 15 teams, each playing 44 regular-season games, producing a total schedule of 330 games in 2026. The report’s reference to 286 games as the current baseline appears to use the previous season’s schedule, when the league had 13 teams. Its longer-term projection anticipates an 18-team league with 468 regular-season games by 2030.The commercial implications extend beyond the additional games themselves. More teams create further opportunities for local sponsorship agreements, while a larger broadcast schedule can give existing partners more chances to reach national audiences. The report’s figures suggest that the value is already being distributed through a combination of league-wide agreements, team partnerships, prominent players and the placement of sponsorship assets across television and social media.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Spurs Dylan Harper slips, leaves game with apparent groin injury
articles.summary: The severity has yet to be announced, but he may miss some time after slipping on the court.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs lost their 12-game win streak Tuesday night at the hands of the Pistons, but they may have lost someone more important to injury.

Second-year guard Dylan Harper went down with just more than a minute left in the game with an apparent groin injury after slipping on a wet spot on the floor. He stayed down while play continued on the other end, and when it finally stopped he had to be helped off the court and back to the locker room.

Coach Mitch Johnson had no update after the game, however, quotes from his teammates suggested Fox may miss some time ( quote via Jared Weiss of The Athletic ).

"At certain parts of [last] season where we didn't have certain guys, that's what made us good, was we were able to cover for guys when they were out," De'Aaron Fox said. "Right now, it looks like we might have to do that again."

Harper has taken a step forward in his second season, averaging 18.4 points on 50.5% shooting, plus 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game — he looks like he will be the second-best Spur in a year or two (if he's not already). He is a very good defender and when he is on the court the Spurs have. +22.3 net rating (and they are in the negative when he is off the court, although some of that is tied to heavy minutes next to Victor Wembanyama).

The Spurs have the depth to withstand Harper being out for a while, it will mean more Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson. However, for the postseason, the Spurs will need Harper, and groin injuries can be tricky and easy to re-injure, so expect San Antonio to be very cautious about bringing him back.

articles.title: Jimtown enters the year with experienced core
articles.summary: ELKHART — Jimtown boys basketball coach Ryan Varga couldn’t have asked for too much more as he opens his second season at the helm in Baugo Township. • Three...
articles.body:
ELKHART — Jimtown boys basketball coach Ryan Varga couldn't have asked for too much more as he opens his second season at the helm in Baugo Township.

• Three talented starters back – all juniors.

• A 6-foot-7 newcomer to protect the rim.

Not a bad start for the Jimmies, who went 15-9 last season, earning runner-up finishes in both the Indiana Northern State Conference and the Class 2A LaVille Sectional.

But that's not to say the losses weren't important.

Will Spurgeon led the Jimmies in scoring last season (17.0), assists and steals, while shooting 82 percent from the free throw line. He was a member of The Truth's All-Area first team. Tra'sean Baldwin, who led the team in rebounds, has also graduated.

The returnees are led by the Jimmies' three-headed monster of juniors, Dominic Fey, Jackson Woolwine and Xander Whitaker.

Fey, listed at 6-foot-3, was an All-Area second team selection last season after averaging 12.1 points, five rebounds and three assists-a-game last season. The 6-1 Whitaker was also a double figure scorer (11.8) and he ranked second in rebounds (6-2).

Wooldwine averaged 9.4 points, while shooting 45 percent from 3-point range and 92 percent from the line.

"Anytime you have three starters back and they'll be you're three main guys, it's exciting,'' Varga admitted. "They all had a really good summer and learned a lot about themselves both offensively and defensively.

"We weren't as physically strong as some of the teams we faced last year. But since June, our kids have been working hard in the weight room and that's a real credit to them.

While Landon Gingerich didn't do a lot of scoring the Jimtown last season, Varga knows he's an important part of the 2026-57 Jimmies.

"He provides a lot of leadership for us,'' Varga said. He's a captain and a glue guy that works to keep everyone calm.

Jimtown also also brought some size into the school, when 6-7 Brayden Harshberger transferred after playing JV at Elkhart last season. In addition, 6-4 junior Oliver Cannon is now at Jimtown after being homeschooled.

"Those at some nice additions for us,'' Varga admitted. "Baldwin did a nice job for us last season inside, but we didn't have the size and physicality we have right now.

"I think with our guys being built stronger now, we should be able to crash the boards and finish around the rim better. Last season, we got bumped around some, I don't think that will happen this year.''

The Jimmies have some experienced depth in senior Tucker Sahlhoff and juniors Max Ganger and Murphy DiPiro. Varga said three freshman could eventually see playing time, including 6-foot guard John Jackson Jr.

Leg by Woolwine and Whitaker (45%), the Jimmies combined to shoot 41 percent from 3-point range last season, a number that could go up this year.

"The 3-points really open the game up for us,'' Varga said. "We shot it well last year and didn't have a real threat inside like we do this year. If we're hitting the 3's, it changes how teams will have to defend us and should open up the lanes and for our guys inside.

"The keys for us will be putting the ball in the basket and getting tougher defensively. There were times last season where we were up 10 or 12 and then we'd get lackadaisical for a couple possessions and all of a sudden it's a six-point game. We need to stay focused for the whole game.''

Jimtown lost the INSC title and the LaVille Sectional titles to Bremen, who will return All-State candidate Chase Devine.

"Bremen is the champions untill someone knocks them off their throne,'' Varga said. "But we can't get ahead of oursleves. We just need to get better every game and play who is in front of us. Right now, our focus is on Prairie Heights for our opener.''

According to Varga, Jimtown will host the Class 2A sectional in March and will also host Bremen in an INSC game.
authors: KEN FOX, The Elkhart Truth, Ind.

articles.title: Rams rumors: ESPN insider opens door to shocking Puka Nacua free agency gambit
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are in a fascinating position on their bye week. LA is 6-4 on the season and riding a four-game winning streak. That is great news afte...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are in a fascinating position on their bye week . LA is 6-4 on the season and riding a four-game winning streak. That is great news after the Rams were incredibly slow out of the gates this fall. But could the Rams be in for some huge changes during the 2027 offseason?

ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler discussed potential 2027 free agents in their latest article. Graziano pitched the idea that Puka Nacua could end up hitting the free market.

"Nacua didn't get the big contract extension that Jaxon Smith-Njigba got last offseason, even though he was eligible," Graziano wrote. "And the Rams don't hold a fifth-year option on him for next year because he wasn't a first-round pick. Nacua also made bad headlines with his off-field behavior in the offseason and could still face league discipline under the personal conduct policy."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Rams are currently set to have $75.27 million in cap space during the 2027 offseason. That could be enough to extend Nacua and still fill out the roster. However, it could mean letting another talented player walk in free agency.

Graziano also cited Nacua's injury history as another reason for concern. Puka is on IR with a knee injury and has dealt with nagging injuries throughout his career. It is fair to question if longevity will be a long-term concern for the superstar receiver.

"He's 25 years old and a brilliant player, but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity," Graziano argued. "All of that is to say: I could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers."

Ultimately, the Rams will likely base their future decisions on how far they get in 2026. Regardless of what direction LA chooses, their decision on Nacua's future will be the most important choice of the offseason.

Next up for the Rams is a Week 12 matchup against the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

articles.title: 3 key stats from Indiana men’s basketball’s 81-76 win over Arkansas
articles.summary: From Darren Harris’ rebounding to Samet Yigitoglu’s scoring, here’s a few notable stats from the win over the Hogs.
articles.body:
Indiana men's basketball logged its first signature non-conference win under second-year head coach Darian DeVries on Tuesday evening, taking down Arkansas 80-79 at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

The Hoosiers' second high-major game of the 2026-27 season proved as thrilling (stressful) as the first. Indiana built up an early lead before letting Arkansas back in, falling behind before taking the lead just before halftime. The second half featured more of the same, with Arkansas taking control with four minutes to go before great shotmaking from Darren Harris and Bryce Lindsay cemented the win.

Here's some key stats that jumped off the page:

Indiana's identity is its rebounding. Darian DeVries emphasized that to the team in practice throughout the summer and in media whenever he was asked about it.

And, of course it is. Indiana's jumbo starting frontcourt of Samet Yigitoglu and Aiden Sherrell are both built to go at the glass with size and strength down low. But you need buy-in from the backcourt as well, and that was readily apparent in Harris' play.

The huge late 3-pointers will be remembered, but Harris finished second on the team with seven rebounds as a guard, one that typically hangs out around the perimeter at that.

Arkansas likes to run. John Calipari built this roster with a ton of young talent that looks to force mistakes on defense and turn said mistakes into quick points at the other end to run teams into the ground.

That didn't happen against Indiana. At all. The Hoosiers mostly turned the Razorbacks into a half-court team, limiting them to just 5 points in fastbreak situations. It was an early worry that this roster, with its big-oriented construction, would have issues guarding up-tempo teams.

The defense performed reliably well, holding Arkansas to 42.1% from the field. There's probably growth to be had there and there aren't many teams built like Arkansas in the sport, but there's positive early signs.

Samet Yigitoglu may be more of a valuable offensive piece than we'd thought heading into the season.

He wasn't featured at SMU and needs some help getting set up, but he has the size to get a pretty good look on just about anyone when he gets the ball in the low post. He finished just 5-11 from the field, but that was mostly because he was getting fouled and finished 7-8 at the free throw line.

Indiana's been trying to get him more looks after a relatively quiet outing against Syracuse and DeVries had mentioned looking to do so even before that game. Arkansas was a particularly good matchup for that as the Razorbacks had no answers for his size. If he can give the team a reliable 12-14 points per night, that changes how teams need to guard Indiana a fair amount.

articles.title: Madrid Daily: Güler renews as JJ Gabriel edges closer to Real Madrid
articles.summary: Mijatović weighs in on Vinícius, Argentina’s youngsters shine, and two former Madrid players announce their retirements.
articles.body:
Real Madrid have confirmed Arda Güler's contract extension, while reports suggest another young talent is approaching a move to Valdebebas. Elsewhere, Pedja Mijatović has discussed Vinícius Júnior's form and future, José Mourinho has reflected on his relationship with the club, and Nico Paz and Franco Mastantuono have enjoyed a productive night with Argentina.

Güler renews until 2032, and Mbappé welcomes the news

Real Madrid have announced that Arda Güler has extended his contract until June 30, 2032 . The Turkish midfielder joined the club in July 2023 and has since made 126 appearances, with five trophies to his name.

Kylian Mbappé was quick to celebrate his teammate's renewal. The Frenchman was the first to publicly share his enthusiasm following the announcement.

JJ Gabriel visits Valdebebas as Madrid move approaches

JJ Gabriel's proposed move to Real Madrid has entered its final stages. According to AS, the 16-year-old visited Valdebebas for an initial meeting and work with the club's medical staff, having already spent several days training individually in Madrid.

The report, citing information from El Chiringuito, puts the payment to Manchester United at approximately €360,000 in training compensation. The move is approaching completion, although an official signing announcement remains pending.

The intended pathway would initially take Gabriel into Juvenil A before a move to Castilla in January. AS explains that the registration window for Castilla and Real Madrid C is currently closed, while the youth registration period remains open. Under the arrangements described in the report, registering with Juvenil A would not allow him to immediately appear for the reserve team.

Gabriel, who turned 16 on October 6, has also joined Epic Sports, the agency headed by Ali Barat, whose clients include Dean Huijsen and Denzel Dumfries.

Madrid's interest follows a series of notable performances in United's academy, including a UEFA Youth League hat-trick against Sabah. AS reports that Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich also showed interest in the youngster, whose anticipated next step is now at La Fábrica.

Mijatović discusses Vinícius's form, competition and future

Pedja Mijatović has urged Vinícius Júnior to make the most of his playing career following the Brazilian's recent comments about his difficult start to the season.

Speaking on Cadena SER's El Larguero after Vinícius's hat-trick against Singapore, the former Madrid player and sporting director questioned whether the forward had allowed himself to become too comfortable.

"I think Vinicius has relaxed, this idea that I have to live because I'm so young… I have to tell him that after leaving football there's so much life to enjoy with family and friends. He's not going to earn as much money as he does now."

Mijatović believes Madrid's eventual assessment of Vinícius will depend heavily on how the season develops, particularly whether the Brazilian recovers his influence in a successful team.

"Real Madrid, as the most important club in the world, which only recognizes success, if this year ends well and if Madrid manages to win La Liga or the Champions League, or both, and if Vinicius is a key player, performs well, recovers well, and is decisive, I think they won't sell him under any circumstances… But if the opposite happens, I think the club will consider any offers that come in. And they will surely come in."

Mijatović also claimed that Madrid had rejected "one or two very important offers" for Vinícius, identifying Arsenal as one of the interested clubs and saying that "Arteta was very keen to see Vinicius in his team." Those comments represent Mijatović's account of the interest and his assessment of Madrid's options.

"I don't want to say they made a mistake, because he's 26 years old and has a lot of potential and a big market, but if Madrid doesn't achieve a major objective, all the players, if a good, significant offer comes in, will be up for sale."

Diomande's emergence increases the competition

Mijatović also pointed to Yan Diomande's performances as an important change in Vinícius's situation.

"This year he has more competition. Football evolves and there is always competition because you can't relax, since there is always a teammate who is more competitive."

Nevertheless, he considered Vinícius's performances during the international break encouraging, while leaving the question of his place in Madrid's starting lineup to Mourinho.

"Whether Vinicius should play or not is something you'd have to ask Mourinho, but the two matches Vini played with the national team are a guarantee that the lad is very eager. The most important thing for a coach like Mourinho is to have such a large squad with very good players who can cover for any absence he might have at any given time."

Mourinho: "I've identified with Real Madrid from day one"

José Mourinho helped inaugurate the 2026–27 academic year at the Real Madrid–Universidad Europea school on Tuesday, appearing alongside Emilio Butragueño.

University rector Elena Gazapo and the school's managing director, Marisa Sáenz, also attended the ceremony welcoming its 21st intake of students. Mourinho used the occasion to discuss his connection with Madrid, his father's affection for the club and the demands of coaching.

"It's one of my homes, but it's my home. That's how I've felt both while I've been here and during the 13 years I wasn't. I've always wanted what's best for the club and the fans' happiness. I've identified with Real Madrid from day one."

Reflecting on his first departure in 2013, Mourinho said that his years elsewhere had strengthened his understanding of Madrid's standing beyond Spain.

"Real Madrid is great because of everything it has won, and also because of its principles and its approach to sports and society. I was away for 13 years, and during that time I gained a better understanding of what people outside of Spain think of Real Madrid. In 2013, I could have stayed, but I left out of love for the club and because I felt that at that time the team didn't need my profile."

Mourinho also recalled his father Félix's admiration for Alfredo Di Stéfano and the significance of playing at the Bernabéu in Gento's testimonial.

"He was in love with Real Madrid and Di Stéfano. He had a wonderful career as a player, and one of the highlights was a friendly at the Bernabéu, Gento's testimonial match. For him and his generation, Di Stéfano was the best of all time. That match meant a lot to the Portuguese because our hero, Eusébio, never left Portuguese football for political reasons, and he played for Real Madrid in that game."

Asked about the foundations of his coaching career, Mourinho emphasized preparation while acknowledging the isolation that can accompany the job.

"It's a combination of factors. I was born with something and I've always prepared myself for the next step. Things seemed to be falling into place. Even though we have many people around us, the coach is always alone, and that's tough. You have to know how to hide your weaknesses."

WATCH: Nico Paz scores twice as Argentina beat Costa Rica 7–0

Nico Paz and Franco Mastantuono each scored twice in Argentina's 7–0 friendly victory over Costa Rica at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium on Tuesday. Julián Álvarez also recorded a brace, with Alexis Mac Allister scoring Argentina's other goal.

Paz opened the scoring with a left-footed finish following a quick passing move involving Álvarez and a backheel from Enzo Fernández. His second was an individual effort: after emerging with the ball from a group of defenders, he fired a right-footed shot into the top corner.

The Como midfielder's two goals came before halftime, with Mastantuono subsequently adding his own double in a comfortable victory for Argentina.

"I am very happy; representing these colors is the ultimate goal. Especially on days like today, with all the people supporting us and all the love that was felt today," Paz said.

With Lionel Messi absent, Paz was also asked about the possibility of eventually wearing Argentina's number 10 shirt. He preferred to focus on the experience of playing for his country.

"The truth is, I don't think about that. What I think about is enjoying and having fun on the pitch because what I love most is playing football, and on top of that representing the national team and so many people."

Erik Lira recalls Bellingham's words after their World Cup encounter

Cruz Azul midfielder Erik Lira has recalled his exchange with Jude Bellingham following Mexico's World Cup round-of-16 meeting with England at the Azteca Stadium.

Speaking on Roberto Martínez's Creativo podcast, Lira described the challenge of facing the Madrid midfielder, who scored twice, and the encouragement he received from him afterward.

"Bellingham came up to me, shook my hand, and I wished him success, 'I hope you become world champions,' and he said to me, 'You're a great player, you have a big heart, I hope you play for a big team.' After that, I ran into him and asked if he had his shirt and if we could swap. He said yes, and I'm leaving with that, with Bellingham's shirt and with him saying that to me."

Lira also described the aggressive mindset he had tried to adopt before the match, explaining how he motivated himself for the assignment of marking Bellingham.

"When I found out it was England, I told myself, 'I'm going to mark Jude Bellingham', top 5 or top 10 best players in the world, incredible, that's when I got mentally prepared, I have to eat him, I have to kick him, I'm going to pull him, I'm going to spit on him, I don't know what the hell I'm going to do to him, and even so he scored two goals against us."

For Lira, the recognition afterward carried considerable weight, even with the disappointment of the result.

"A lot of people told me I ate Jude Bellingham alive, but damn, he scored two goals against us; they weren't my responsibility, because it was everyone's. But having him close by and having him tell me at the end of the game 'you're a great player'; I cried, yes I cried, not too much, but it was like saying that's how I wanted to lose, giving it my all, to the limit, it helps me and it doesn't hurt so much."

Former Madrid academy midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement at 38, bringing an end to a career that included World Cup and European Championship success with Spain, major European trophies at club level and a final chapter in Australia.

Reflecting on the motivation that sustained him throughout his career, Mata emphasized the everyday enjoyment of playing.

"It's been so many years thanks to the enjoyment I get from the game. Waking up every morning eager to train, to play, whether in magnificent settings like Old Trafford, Stamford Bridge or Mestalla… or in my early days at the Juventud Estadio, where the pitch turned into a mud pit every winter. I think that passion is fundamental to everything in life."

After progressing through Madrid's academy, Mata established himself at Valencia, where he won the Copa del Rey. At Chelsea, he lifted the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup, before adding further silverware during his time at Manchester United. His international honours include the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012.

Mata's later career took him to Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe before spells with Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

Antonio Adán also brings his career to a close

Antonio Adán has announced his retirement at 39. The former Madrid academy goalkeeper went on to play for Cagliari, Real Betis, Atlético Madrid, Sporting CP and, most recently, Esteghlal.

"After much thought, I want to announce that I am retiring from professional football."

In his farewell message, Adán thanked the people and clubs who had accompanied him throughout his career.

"I have been fortunate enough to experience everything I dreamed of as a child. I have won, I have lost, I have cried, and I have celebrated, and above all, I have learned. Thank you to everyone who gave me the opportunity, to all the teammates who walked alongside me, to the coaches who taught me, to the clubs that were my home and my family for always being there."

Adán concluded by reflecting on the familiar sounds of a goalkeeper's working life, from the ball striking a post to the atmosphere in the dressing room before a match.

"Football has given me everything, and although I will no longer be able to hear those sounds, I know for sure that they will remain etched in my memory. Thank you, football. It has been a privilege."

articles.title: Nike puts three high school football powerhouses in star-studded promo video
articles.summary: Mater Dei, St. John Bosco and The St. James Academy joined some of sports' biggest names in a Nike promo video narrated by Oregon coach Dan Lanning.
articles.body:
"Time to turn the doubters into believers."

Those were just a few of the words of Oregon head football coach Dan Lanning , whose voice narrated a Nike video featuring some of the biggest names in sports — and three prominent high school athletic programs.

The St. James Performance Academy (VA), Mater Dei (CA) , and St. John Bosco (CA) were among three high schools featured in the montage on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at Nike's Investor Day in Portland.

The video, which introduced Nike CEO Elliott Hill during the company's Investor Day, included a slew of professional athletes in Michael Jordan, Cristiano Ronaldo, LeBron James, Kobe Bryant, Serena Williams, Erling Haaland, Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, Naomi Osaka, Victor Wembanyama, Luka Dončić, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jayson Tatum, Caitlin Clark, Jalen Hurts, Sabrina Ionescu, Jalen Brunson, Sha'Carri Richardson, CeeDee Lamb and Christian Yelich.

The inclusion of three high school programs offered a notable spotlight for institutions with different athletic identities and plenty happening as the 2026 season approaches its conclusion.

For The St. James Performance Academy, the exposure comes during a significant stretch for its young football program.

The Strivers, ranked 12th in the latest USA TODAY Super 25 rankings , were recently selected to compete in the second annual Overtime Nationals. They will face Bishop Gorman of Las Vegas on Dec. 9. The matchup will be televised on ESPN2, with the winning school receiving a $200,000 donation and the runner-up earning $100,000.

In just its second season, The St. James has already drawn attention through its performances against established national programs. The Strivers narrowly lost to IMG Academy (Bradenton, FL) , 44-42, in October before earning a 28-20 victory over St. Frances Academy (Baltimore, MD).

Mater Dei, meanwhile, is navigating a major transition.

The California powerhouse announced Tuesday, Nov. 17, that head football coach Raul Lara will not return after three seasons. Lara compiled a 29-6 record, including a perfect 13-0 campaign in 2024 that ended with a national championship.

The Monarchs finished 8-3 in 2026, with their season ending in a 45-15 loss to Centennial (CA) in the CIF Southern Section Division 1 quarterfinals, making the worst loss for the program since Sept. 17, 2010, also to Centennial. Assistant Randy Wright has been named interim coach as the school begins its search for a replacement.

St. John Bosco, however, remains in the hunt for a Southern Section championship.

The Braves, ranked 21st in the USA TODAY Super 25 , advanced to the CIF Southern Section Division 1 semifinals following a 38-0 victory over Orange Lutheran. Bosco will face the nation's top team in No. 1 Santa Margarita on Friday, Nov. 20, with a spot in the championship game at stake.

The Braves have consistently been one of the country's premier high school football programs, with their rivalry against Mater Dei helping define the Southern California high school football landscape.

Three programs with different paths, traditions and immediate storylines now share a place in a Nike video alongside some of the most recognizable athletes in the world. Lanning closed with a powerful message, one that could strike a chord with those three programs.

"Are you going to prove them right, or wrong?" Lanning asked. "When they say you're too big, are you going to show them they're thinking small? Think it's time to tell the truth. This time is yours, and you know exactly how this goes. You've been here before. This is muscle memory, folks.

"Time to turn the doubters into believers. Time to turn the tide, land the blow, sink the dagger. Time to prove you are who you say you are. Who you've been and always will be. There's no time for 'time will tell.' Because that time, because that time, is now."

articles.title: Insider explains why Commanders could still want Brandon Aiyuk
articles.summary: The 49ers may have moved on from Brandon Ayiuk, but there's a chance the Commanders might still be interested.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders may not be done with Brandon Aiyuk just yet. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels have reconciled after a rocky summer, which could leave the door open for a reunion if the San Francisco 49ers release their disgruntled receiver.

Aiyuk, reinstated by the NFL and currently on a two-week roster exemption while he sorts out forfeiture money owed to San Francisco, took aim at Daniels and his mother, Regina Jackson, as part of a run of social media posts over the summer. That strained a relationship that was once strong dating back to their days at Arizona State. According to Fowler, though, Aiyuk reached out to Daniels about a month ago, who was receptive and understanding. Fowler said it's unclear what the reconciliation means for Aiyuk's chances of playing in Washington, but "he and the quarterback are good again."

Speculation about a Commanders fit lingered all year, with the idea that Washington would be interested if the 49ers moved on from Aiyuk. Earlier reports indicated the team would only pursue him if he were released rather than traded. Those reports soured during the summer, when Aiyuk criticized the 49ers and was also seen in Commanders gear, before he reportedly turned on Daniels and his family.

After Aiyuk was reinstated, ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that the Commanders aren't expected to be in the market for him.

Still, there's a case for the fit. Washington lost Terry McLaurin to a season-ending knee injury but remains in the hunt for the NFC East title. Aiyuk could help fill the void if he's healthy and truly interested in playing. And given his connection to Daniels, he could seamlessly fit back into the offense despite not playing since he tore his ACL in Week 7 of the 2024 season.

The 49ers, meanwhile, have mentally moved on. Their roster exemption for Aiyuk expires after Week 11, which means they'll have to either release him or make room for him on the 53-man roster.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns Predicted to Replace Deshaun Watson With Dual-Threat QB
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are battling for a playoff spot but could still move on from Deshaun Watson as they are mocked to select a QB. The post Cleveland Browns...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are battling for a playoff spot but could still move on from Deshaun Watson.

Watson won the Browns starting quarterback job, and he's performed well, as he's helped Cleveland get into the playoff mix.

The Browns are coming off a thrilling comeback win over the Houston Texans and are on their bye week.

Cleveland Browns Mocked to Select LaNorris Sellers

Cleveland has two first-round picks and could use one of them to find their franchise quarterback.

The Browns are a young team, but they still need to find their franchise quarterback, which they could do this offseason. Although Watson has played well, he's a pending free agent, so his future is up in the air.

With that, ESPN NFL analyst Jordan Reid has the Browns selecting LaNorris Sellers out of South Carolina to be the franchise quarterback.

"Deshaun Watson has seen a slight resurgence this season. But the plan all along has been for the Browns to draft a younger quarterback to be the long-term answer," Reid wrote . "Sellers is a bit of a wild card, as he was getting first-round hype entering the 2025 campaign before struggling during the season. He has rallied this season as an explosive, dual-threat QB with A-level attributes and has made strides as a passer, particularly since midseason.

"Sellers is still a bit polarizing for NFL scouts, who have expressed a wide range of outcomes on where they think he'll be drafted, but the league values his athletic tools. I could see a team such as the Browns, who have two first-round picks, taking a chance on him at this point of Round 1."

Sellers is a dual-threat quarterback who has a good arm and can also extend plays with his legs. He's in his third year as South Carolina's starter and has boosted his draft stock. He's thrown for 2,100 yards, 17 touchdowns, and 7 interceptions this season, while also rushing for 637 yards and 7 touchdowns.

Cleveland Has Decision to Make on Deshaun Watson

Although Cleveland is mocked to select a quarterback, they still could bring back Watson.

Watson is a pending free agent, and Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot believes the team could bring him back.

"Things have been so good with Watson this season, the Browns should re-sign him after the season," Cabot said. "They've been criss-crossing the country watching college quarterbacks all season. And will likely draft one in the first round with one or both of their first-round picks. But the Browns should bring back Watson to build on what he's accomplished this season, and to hit the ground running in 2027."

Even if the Browns re-sign Watson, that doesn't rule out the team selecting a quarterback.

articles.title: Hawaii’s Victoria Leyva heads home to El Paso but focused on team goals
articles.summary: In between senior night and the Mountain West Conference tournament, Hawaii’s Victoria Leyva gets a homecoming of her own. The Rainbow Wahine’s final two mat...
articles.body:
In between senior night and the Mountain West Conference tournament, Hawaii's Victoria Leyva gets a homecoming of her own.

The Rainbow Wahine's final two matches of the regular season today and Thursday against UTEP take place in Leyva's hometown of El Paso, Texas, where the junior libero prepped at Pebble Hills High School, roughly 25 miles away.

When the announcement was made that both Hawaii and UTEP were moving conferences to the MWC in almost all sports, Leyva immediately realized she would get to play in front of some special people in her life.

"I'm super excited. I have grandparents that haven't been able to see me play collegiate volleyball," Leyva said. "I have family and friends that were never going to see me play collegiate volleyball. It's all been through TV, so being able to go back and see them supporting me in the stands and living out my dream is just extra special."

After defeating Air Force on senior night Friday, the women's volleyball team left early Monday morning to finish out the regular season on a rare Wednesday/Thursday back-to-back.

Hawaii (23-4, 15-1) already knows it will be the No. 1 seed in the Credit Union 1 Mountain West Women's Volleyball Championship and will play in the semifinals at 11 a.m. on Tuesday against the No. 4 seed at The Pavilion in Las Vegas.

UTEP (16-12, 8-8), which hosts UH at 3 p.m. at Memorial Gym today and Thursday, is in fifth place in the conference, one match behind New Mexico.

The Miners would need to beat UH at least once and hope the Lobos lose twice to have a shot to slide into the fourth spot.

Leyva doesn't want any part of helping out her hometown school.

"For us, we want to finish out strong," Leyva said. "Our biggest thing is still continuing to build up on our game. We took care of Air Force in three (on Friday) and we want to be able to go up to El Paso and take care of everything with consistency and discipline and continue to build on that, because we want to be as great as we can to win the tournament and continue to build to the NCAA Tournament."

Hawaii moved back into the top 40 at No. 38 in the latest NCAA RPI rankings released Monday.

UH's regular-season championship is its first since 2022 in the Big West, but does not guarantee a spot in the NCAA Tournament.

UH has to win the tourney to earn an automatic bid. It is in a decent spot in the RPI rankings to contended for an at-large berth, but nobody wants to leave up their postseason possibility to a selection committee.

"Our goals are higher than just obviously winning the (conference) tournament. We want to get to the NCAA Tournament," Hawaii coach Joshua Walker said. "Our ability to go into a tough environment and play well enough to win (at UTEP) puts ourselves in a position to do it again next week."

The team will stay on the mainland and head to Las Vegas to prepare for the tournament this weekend.

The Rainbow Wahine are the only team to have clinched their exact seeding in the tournament.

Grand Canyon (11-5) is one match ahead of UC Davis (10-6) for second place and the two teams play this weekend.

The Lopes, who have won eight in a row, have clinched a berth in the tournament, while the Aggies still need either a win or a loss by the Miners.

Wyoming needs to win both matches against New Mexico to have a chance at the fourth spot.

"For us we try to just focus on our side of the net," Walker said. "We practiced Sunday, we traveled (Monday), we did our scout (Tuesday) and (today) we will do a little bit more video and have our match. We try to keep the schedule as similar as possible every time we travel so the athletes have that familiarity. Our ability to try to keep things the same and have the same business trip every time we go out is important."

The team will spend an extra day in El Paso before heading to Las Vegas, giving Leyva the opportunity to take the team to the one place she is looking forward to eating the most.

"There's this place called Chico's Tacos," Leyva said. "They are famous for their little rolled tacos. They're called flautas. Plus they got this special sauce. It's a delicious place that hits great late night."

articles.title: Ben Johnson thinks things aren’t what they seem with Bears offense
articles.summary: Chicago's head coach identifies a key area needing improvement.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson believes there is more to his team's rushing statistics than meets the eye, suggesting one popular NFL metric doesn't accurately reflect the offense's performance this season.

The Bears are averaging 4.2 yards per rushing attempt through the 2026 campaign, matching the league-wide average. However, Johnson believes that number can be misleading, particularly when considering how frequently Chicago runs the football in short-yardage and red-zone situations.

Speaking about the team's rushing production, Johnson explained why he isn't overly concerned with the statistic.

"I don't see it as bigger chunk runs, necessarily. The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways," Johnson said. "We run the ball a lot in the red zone, and when you're down there a four-yard carry is really an explosive."

Johnson wants more efficiency from Bears rushing attack

While Johnson doesn't believe yards per carry tells the entire story, that doesn't mean he is completely satisfied with Chicago's ground game.

The head coach explained that an occasional long run can inflate a team's average, while shorter attempts in important situations can bring that number down. For example, a one-yard gain on fourth-and-goal from the one-yard line can negatively affect an offense's overall average despite accomplishing exactly what the team needs.

Instead, Johnson places greater importance on consistency and efficiency.

Chicago currently has a 49.2 percent rushing success rate, a figure that Johnson believes needs to improve.

"We go off efficiency, and we're under 50 percent efficient running the ball. We set our bar higher than that," he said.

Bears look to maintain momentum after bye week

Despite Johnson's concerns about the running game, Chicago has enjoyed an impressive start to the season.

The Bears enter Week 11 with a 7-2 record after receiving a bye in Week 10. They will now look to continue their strong campaign when they host the New Orleans Saints (3-6) on Sunday.

Johnson clearly believes there is room for improvement offensively, particularly when it comes to establishing a more consistent rushing attack.

With Chicago firmly in the playoff picture, improving its efficiency on the ground could become an important factor as the team enters the second half of the season.
