articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs wins second NFC offensive player of the week award of the season
articles.summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich.
articles.body:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich.

Now the league has recognized him for his performance in that contest.

Gibbs has been named NFC offensive player of the week.

Gibbs put up 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing, 99 receiving) along with two rushing touchdowns in the 35-10 win.

According to the league, Gibbs is just the second player under the age of 25 in NFL history with at least 250 yards from scrimmage and two rushing touchdowns in multiple games, joining Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson. He also scored his 61st and 62nd touchdowns, which puts him past Hall of Famer Terrell Davis for the most touchdowns by a player in his first four seasons in league history.

The 252 yards were the most by a player in a single game so far this season. They were also the second most in an international game in league history.

Gibbs now has five career offensive player of the week awards. He last won it for Week 5 of this year.

Through nine games, Gibbs leads the league with 1,000 rushing yards, 1,384 yards from scrimmage, 11 rushing touchdowns, and 13 total TDs.

articles.title: Texas A&M Has a Leadership Problem
articles.summary: And it can only be solved by the folks at the very top. The Micro The news of Trev Alberts accepting the Michigan athletic director job certainly caught me o...
articles.body:
And it can only be solved by the folks at the very top.

The news of Trev Alberts accepting the Michigan athletic director job certainly caught me off guard. I appreciate what Trev did for us, the PlayFly deal was a really good set up for A&M and he seemed like he was a good steward of our resources. The hire of Bucky McMillan seems to be paying off, with the other hires TBD. On the other hand, there has been speculation that Schloss's departure could have been handled better…and Baseball as a whole isnt quite as good as when he found it and football is currently 4-6. So ultimately, I'm sad to see him go but also I'm fine with it. Trev strikes me as a change agent kind of guy, someone who is built to burn bright but not long and I appreciate him for his time here.

There are trends and patterns that we need to pay attention to. At the AD level we've now lost three guys…Woodward, Bjork, and Trev to other power 5 schools who have a higher level of esteem than us (much to our own chagrin). Maybe our athletic department is a stepping stone because the trend of three guys looking at LSU, Ohio State, and Michigan as a step up says as much. This makes 3 different ADs (including RC's time as interim) in the past 5 years.

But bigger than that, this trend reflects the unstable, and inconsistent nature of leadership at Texas A&M. We're working on our 5th (including interim) president in the last 5 years. We can talk all day about why each individual person had to leave or mitigating circumstances associated with their departure, but 5 presidential transitions in 5 years is more than any other program in the country (Florida is right behind us at 4). It is impossible to create any sustainable momentum as an athletic department with this much churn and turnover.

The lack of consistent leadership at key executive levels has led to rash decision making to the tune more than a 125 million dollars of committed money for two coaches, one of whom was fired and the other in the middle of a losing season. We worship at the alter of cutting edge facilities as a way to demonstrate our commitment to excellence…when in actuality excellence is quiet and takes place through steady, firm, values driven leadership. We are desperate for sustained success and stable excellence but we act rashly and out of fear of our coaches leaving.

The reality is that this kind of leadership means circumstances have to be absolutely perfect for us to succeed at the level to which we think we're capable of. Things have to go exactly right in order for us to have an "elite" season and maybe it only happens once every 5-7 years…and guess what. That's exactly who we are. It's not a surprise that we're a "lightening in a bottle" type of program, it's who we have set ourselves up to be.

I've never been one to blame people. I dont care if someone says "it's my fault". I recognize the importance of both, but those, to me, are rear view thinking comments. I want someone to take responsibility and to recognize it's in their purview to fix things. In my view we have a flawed culture of decision making at the highest levels, which rests squarely on the Board of Regents. When we look at continuity, many of the folks on the Board have been there for almost a decade. But during their watch, A&M has seen tremendous churn and turnover. That's an issue. It cant be the fault of the coach because we've changed that. It cant be on the AD because well we've changed that too. It cant be the president because…well we've changed there. Ultimately it's about the context and culture that these folks have operated in and that context and culture is driven by our Board of Regents.

Our Board is made up of competent folks who are likely much smarter and more accomplished than me. But they HAVE to recognize their impact on how our programs are operating right now and operate differently. There is a culture of dogmatic decision making and black and white thinking which results in high turnover, a constant state of interim leadership all over campus, and stagnation. You can either live in a state of circumstance where you are reacting to what goes on around you or you can live in a state of Vision. We value the latter but spend all our time in the former.

Two of the statues A&M has on campus are Sully and Rudder. These two folks made difficult decisions to look beyond what A&M was at that time to what it could be and they made a lot of people mad about the decisions they made…but that tough forward thinking revolutionary paradigm made A&M what it is today. Yet generations later we revel in their shadow, while trying to maintain tradition and make sure things dont change too much. We deify Rudder and Sul Ross without learning from the legacy they left.

Another issue I have is that I've seen us plan effectively. When I was a student our campus was a mish mash of architectural styles that reflected periods of growth followed by periods of stagnation. There was no consistency, or coherency, despite there being an institutional master plan in the late 80s focused on student experience that did not address the physical campus. In 2004 Texas A&M created a campus physical master plan, and that master plan has been adapted and built upon, and we're now starting to see the campus make sense. We've gone from the Spence Park metal gym equipment to Aggie Park. The buildings aren't just soviet bloc architecture, they make sense next to each other. We have values and those values help us make decisions on what comes next. The people who created that master plan recognized the value in creating something that set the groundwork for the next folks to make decisions….they built plans that would outlast them and could be built upon. We've done this with our physical campus, yet we seem unable to do it in the systemic decision making processes that impact our athletic programs.

It is not about one president or one AD. It is about a concerning trend related to the overall governance of Texas A&M. We cannot sit here and be surprised that our football program has a difficult time sustaining relevance when the decision making environment surrounding it is full of chaos and churn. Buddy I get that it's not the Board of Regents fault that Elko hired Wiggins and Lynch. But we have to consider the environment created where a football coach is empowered to do whatever they think fit despite all evidence supporting the notion that it might not be the best idea.

Texas A&M needs sustained, calm, principled leadership at the highest levels. In essence, Texas A&M is a big ass sailboat. We spend so much money on the biggest sails money can buy to take us wherever the wind might go and to operate in reaction to however fast that wind might be blowing. But in the grand scheme of things it doesn't matter how big the sails we raise are if we dont have a functional compass or rudder.

articles.title: Bill Belichick leaves UNC quarterback situation in the air
articles.summary: With a game against UVA rapidly approaching, the Wisconsin transfer's status remains unknown
articles.body:
Last weekend saw the North Carolina Tar Heels suffer multiple setbacks in their conquest for their first bowl since 2024.

Not only did UNC fall in yet another heart-wrenching 16-14 loss against the Louisville Cardinals , but just minutes into the second half, starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. went down with an injury that sidelined him for the remainder of UNC's fourth one-score loss of the season.

When speaking with the media on Monday, head coach Bill Belichick vaguely answered reporters' questions over Edwards' health.

"Getting better. We'll just take it day by day. We're not practicing today, so there's really no evaluation today. We'll see how things are tomorrow and take it from there."

With games against UVA and NC State remaining on the docket, there is a real chance Belichick defies the early-season doubt and carries the Heels to a bowl game, but their chances are stunted without the Wisconsin transfer.

If Edwards is a no-go for this weekend's trip to Scott Stadium, freshman Travis Burgess would presumably be given the reins.

In Burgess' time on the field against the Cardinals, the former four-star recruit notched 59 yards on a 54.5% completion rate, throwing an interception off of a bobbled fourth-down pass to seal the Tar Heels ' record at 5-5 for the season.

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski gives Fernando Mendoza honest verdict after first start for Raiders
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza's composure and potential earns him praise after his NFL starting debut.
articles.body:
Rob Gronkowski has shared his assessment of Fernando Mendoza following the rookie quarterback's first NFL start with the Las Vegas Raiders.

Mendoza made his starting debut against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. The Raiders lost 21-13, but the No. 1 overall pick received praise from Gronkowski and Julian Edelman.

Speaking on The Gronk & Jules Show, Gronkowski gave Mendoza a B-minus grade for his performance.

"I like his demeanor. I like how he handles himself. He looks like a pro-style quarterback. He looks like he belongs," Gronkowski said.

The former Patriots tight end also praised Mendoza's mobility and decision-making. He highlighted the rookie's rushing touchdown, which reminded him of a similar play from Indiana's national championship game.

"He tricked Seattle's defense with the QB draw. It just looked like a great play. He's fast. He's quick. He can read defenses as well," Gronkowski added.

However, Gronkowski also acknowledged the difficult circumstances surrounding Mendoza's debut. Brock Bowers suffered an injury during the opening drive, leaving the rookie without a major offensive weapon.

Gronkowski believes the Raiders need to improve their receiving group and running game around Mendoza.

Julian Edelman gives Fernando Mendoza a higher grade

Edelman disagreed with Gronkowski's initial assessment and gave Mendoza an A-minus. The former Patriots receiver highlighted Mendoza's early accuracy and ability to protect the football.

"He starts five for five on third down, nine for 10 in his first 10 throws," Edelman said. "He took care of the football… doesn't have any horsepower. What's he supposed to do?"

Gronkowski eventually agreed to meet Edelman halfway, settling on a B-plus grade. He said, "How about we meet in the middle, Jules? I said B-minus. You said A-minus. How about we give him a B+?"

He also praised Mendoza for finishing without a turnover during his first start.

"Most importantly, no turnovers," Gronkowski said. "That's huge. That means he's coached well. That means he understands the game clearly already, and it's just his first career start. He's got a bright future.

"What I really love about him the most is he's got juice. He's got presence. That's what it's all about… He's got aura. He looked like he belonged on the football field… like he belonged as the starting quarterback. And that's what you want to see."

Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards without an interception. He also recorded 22 rushing yards and a touchdown. The Raiders dropped to 4-6 after the defeat. They will face the Denver Broncos in Week 11 on November 22.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev faces new civil lawsuit over ‘false allegation’ in domestic abuse case
articles.summary: The lawsuit concerns comments Zverev made in an interview with L’Equipe earlier this year
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev is facing a new civil lawsuit over an alleged "false factual assertion" regarding a domestic abuse case against him.

Brenda Patea, his former partner, filed a lawsuit in a Berlin court on 18 September seeking an injunction and financial compensation over comments Zverev made in an interview earlier this year.

Patea and Zverev settled out of court in 2024 after she accused him of domestic abuse, which he denied. Initially he was served a penalty order – which occurs under German law where the evidence for one side is considered compelling and a trial deemed unnecessary – and fined, before Zverev appealed the decision. The resulting criminal trial was discontinued when the pair settled.

The settlement ordered Zverev to pay €200,000 to charity and to the German state, and stated: "The decision is not a verdict and it is not a decision about guilt or innocence."

However, Zverev told French outlet L'Equipe in an interview this June that Patea's allegations had "been proven false" and that his "innocence had been proven", which Patea's new lawsuit alleges violates the terms of their settlement regarding what public statements can be made about the legal proceedings.

Her lawsuit argues that it is not true that Zverev was proven innocent and that his claims to that are a "false factual assertion", rather than an expression of opinion.

The suit, first reported by Bounces , states: "The defendant does not merely give the impression that he considers himself innocent or assesses the status of the proceedings as favorable to him. Rather, he conveys the statement — presented as an objectively established fact — that his innocence in the criminal proceedings has been proven.

"…The assertion is untrue. There is no court order establishing the defendant's innocence, no final acquittal, or any other decision with corresponding content."

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, told AP : "Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form. Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement." Scheele also said Zverev's assertions had "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client".

Anna Sophie Heuchemer, a lawyer representing Zverev, told The Athletic : "This is nothing more than an expression of opinion, protected by the freedom of speech," adding Zverev's remarks were "a permissible assessment of legal proceedings that have already reached a final, binding conclusion."

Zverev's lawyers confirmed he had been formally served the suit on Wednesday.

Patea, with whom Zverev shares a five-year-old daughter, was the second of two former partners to accuse Zverev of domestic abuse, alleging that he pushed her against a wall and choked her during an argument in 2020. Zverev has always denied the accusations against him.

articles.title: High school football: 4A championship preview, Skyline hoping to deny undefeated Ridgeline a state title repeat
articles.summary: High school football: 4A championship preview, Skyline hoping to deny undefeated Ridgeline a state title repeat
articles.body:
No. 6 Skyline (10-3) vs. No. 1 Ridgeline (13-0)

Friday, Nov. 20, 6:30 p.m., at the University of Utah

Skyline started the season 1-3. All three losses came outside 4A: 14-10 to Stansbury, 45-3 to 6A Lone Peak and 42-7 at Skyridge, which plays for the 6A title earlier the same day. The Eagles haven't lost since. In Brandon Matich's first season, they went 6-0 to win Region 10 outright, then won three playoff games in a row. The first was a 49-19 win over Pine View. In the quarterfinals they beat Provo 23-20 on a field goal with two seconds left.

In the semifinals they beat No. 2 seed Hurricane 24-21. They are the lowest seed left in the bracket, and they're playing in their first title game since they won the 2005 championship.

Jonah Mailei, who ran for 127 yards against Hurricane, said reaching this point has been emotional.

"As soon as that final whistle blew, I was breaking down. I was thinking of all the times that it may have felt hopeless, but now I'm living the dream," he said.

Skyline: What the Eagles need to do to win

Skyline's plan against Hurricane should work against Ridgeline too: run the ball and keep the other offense off the field. "Ridgeline is a really good team obviously and we're going to have to keep the ball in our hands and score fast," Mailei said.

Mailei has run for 1,150 yards and 10 touchdowns at 7.5 yards per carry. Judah Valle has 14 total touchdowns: nine rushing, three receiving and two on kick returns. Tate Johnson has thrown for 2,287 yards and 18 touchdowns and run for eight more. Will Finau averages 22.9 yards per catch. David Campbell caught the winning touchdown against Hurricane, and he also has seven sacks on defense.

The defense forces turnovers. Skyline has 16 interceptions and six defensive touchdowns, and it has scored four more touchdowns on returns. Liam Whitworth has four interceptions and a defensive touchdown. Finau and Adam Fredrick have three interceptions each. Aniti Paiva leads the team with 77 tackles. The Eagles allow 18.3 points per game, fifth in 4A.

Skyline will probably need a few takeaways or a return touchdown to win, and it can't afford to give the ball away itself. Johnson has thrown 12 interceptions, and Ridgeline's defense has 50 sacks. The two common opponents favor Ridgeline. It beat Highland 50-24, and Skyline won that game 37-23. Ridgeline beat Stansbury 42-39, and Skyline lost to the Stallions. "Ridgeline is a powerhouse, and I have all the respect in the world for them," said Matich, who won two state titles at East. "We got our hands full. We'll be ready to go."

Ridgeline has not lost since the 2024 season. The defending 4A champions are 13-0 and have won 27 straight games. Only Stansbury has come within two touchdowns of them this season. The RiverHawks have outscored three playoff opponents 130-34. In the semifinals they scored all 35 of their points in the first half of a 35-10 win over Crimson Cliffs, the 2023 and 2024 champion. Colton Clark blocked a punt and returned it for a touchdown in that game.

Coach Travis Cox said his team doesn't need anything new for the final. "We got to be us," he said. "Whenever you get to the state championship, you don't change who you are, you go with what got you there."

Noah Fiefia set the state single-season record for rushing touchdowns in the first round, and he has kept adding to it. He has 2,692 rushing yards and 46 rushing touchdowns at 10.3 yards per carry. With seven touchdown catches, he has 53 total touchdowns. He ran for 161 yards and three touchdowns against Crimson Cliffs. Hudson Parry averages 10 yards per carry and has 10 total touchdowns. Crew Cox has thrown for 2,170 yards and 26 touchdowns with seven interceptions. Owen Leishman has 1,018 receiving yards and 12 touchdown catches. Ridgeline averages 45.9 points per game, the most in 4A.

The defense allows 15.4 points per game, second in 4A behind Hurricane. It has 50 sacks. Johnathan Groll has 13, and Tye Paskett and Leishman have eight each. Jaxon Zollinger has 106 tackles and Hunter Sholly has 101. Riley Fairbanks and Clark have four interceptions each.

Ridgeline needs to do what it did against Crimson Cliffs: control the line of scrimmage early and build a lead before Skyline's ball-control plan can take hold. The Eagles want a short, close game decided by turnovers. If Fiefia gets going early and Cox protects the ball, Skyline would have to play from behind, and its offense isn't built for that. A win would give Ridgeline back-to-back titles and its third championship, after 2021 and 2025.

Rushing leaders: Jonah Mailei (153 carries, 1,150 yards, 10 TDs), Judah Valle (49 carries, 372 yards, 9 TDs), Tate Johnson (59 carries, 313 yards, 8 TDs)

Receiving leaders: Will Finau (29 rec., 664 yards, 8 TDs), Judah Valle (36 rec., 496 yards, 3 TDs), David Campbell (19 rec., 326 yards, 3 TDs)

Tackles leaders: Aniti Paiva (77 tackles), Heamasi Nau (59 tackles), Liam Whitworth (54 tackles), Xander Mattinson (54 tackles)

articles.title: Rangers get huge Corey Seager update that is a big change in trade rumors
articles.summary: This is a huge change for the Rangers and the trade rumors surrounding Seager.
articles.body:
The 2026-2027 MLB offseason for the Texas Rangers might not be the exciting one that some other teams around baseball will have.

Instead of this Rangers team making a massive addition, it seems that a massive subtraction is very much in play. That subtraction could come in the form of the departure of Corey Seager.

According to ESPN's Jeff Passan , Seager is a legitimate trade candidate, especially now that he's reportedly willing to waive his no-trade clause to some select teams.

Corey Seager changes mind, opens door to trade from Rangers

"Texas shortstop Corey Seager, whom the Rangers are open to moving," Passan writes. "... Seager has indicated an openness to moving, but it's to fewer than a handful of teams, and there is no current momentum on a deal."

There is a path that's now been opened to the Rangers to trade away Seager at some point this offseason. This report is a massive step towards a deal being completed.

With Seager's full no-trade clause, the Rangers could only trade him if he decides he wants to be dealt to a new franchise. So far, that's not been the case.

However, with this new report from Passan that Seager is willing to waive his no-trade clause in only a few circumstances, a deal is a lot more possible than it's ever been.

There is no clear indication of which teams are on Seager's mind as destinations he'd accept a trade to. The Atlanta Braves would seem to be an obvious fit as a World Series contender in need of a shortstop like Seager.

But would Seager waive his no-trade clause to go to Atlanta? It's possible, especially if Seager is looking to contend on a team while not being the lone superstar on the roster.

A trade isn't guaranteed, and it's more likely he remains in Texas than not. But this report has opened the door to a deal, as Seager has a very short list of teams he'd be open to moving to this offseason.

articles.title: Ben Duckett stars with 133 as England thrash Australia by 97 runs to win ODI series in Hobart
articles.summary: In a thrilling conclusion to the ODI series, England triumphed over Australia in Hobart, clinching the victory with impressive performances. Ben Duckett shon...
articles.body:
England defeated Australia by 97 runs in the third and deciding ODI in Hobart on Wednesday to clinch the three-match series 2-1. Ben Duckett starred with a brilliant century, while young pacer Sonny Baker produced an impressive bowling performance to help the visitors seal a comprehensive victory. After England captain Harry Brook elected to bat, the visitors posted 328 in 48.3 overs. Australia, in reply, were bowled out for 231 in 46.5 overs, falling well short of their target.

Ben Duckett leads England's batting charge

Duckett anchored England's innings with a magnificent 133 off 115 deliveries, hitting 15 fours and three sixes. He shared an opening stand of 74 runs with Tom Banton, who contributed 44 off 35 balls. The left-hander survived two dropped chances before making the most of his opportunities. Despite losing partners at regular intervals, Duckett continued to build the innings and brought up his seventh ODI century with a single off Cooper Connolly. Matt Renshaw eventually ended his knock, with Josh Inglis completing the catch behind the stumps. Will Jacks provided the late impetus with a valuable 59 off 48 balls, helping England cross the 300-run mark. Jack Edwards was Australia's most successful bowler with four wickets for 31 runs, while Renshaw picked up three wickets.

Chasing 329, Australia suffered an early collapse as Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head were dismissed inside the first 10 deliveries. Josh Inglis also departed cheaply as the hosts slipped to 34/3. Matt Renshaw and Alex Carey attempted to steady the innings with a crucial partnership. Renshaw scored 55, while Carey contributed 37, but Liam Dawson broke the stand by dismissing the former. Carey was subsequently run out, leaving Australia in trouble once again. Cooper Connolly (29) and Jack Edwards (31) offered some resistance, but the lower order failed to mount a serious challenge. Cameron Green also had to retire hurt after being struck on the helmet by a delivery from Gus Atkinson. Oliver Peake came in as his concussion substitute but managed only five runs.

Sonny Baker, Liam Dawson star with the ball

Sonny Baker led England's bowling attack with figures of 4/45 in 10 overs, while Liam Dawson claimed three wickets for 42 runs. Jack Edwards scored 31, but Australia's innings eventually ended at 231 in 46.5 overs, handing England a 97-run victory. England clinch series ahead of T20I challenge England bounced back from their defeat in the opening ODI in Perth to win the next two matches and secure the series 2-1. The visitors will carry the momentum into the upcoming five-match T20I series, which begins in Melbourne on Saturday.

articles.title: Jaelan Phillips wins first NFC defensive player of the week award
articles.summary: The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday.

Now one of their players has been recognized for his performance in the win.

Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips has been named NFC defensive player of the week.

Phillips had five total tackles with three for loss, a sack, and a fumble recovery that led to a Panthers touchdown in the 20-17 victory.

According to the league, Phillips is the second player in the conference to have three TFLs and a fumble recovery in a single game in 2026.

This is Phillips' first career defensive player of the week award.

In his first season with Carolina, Phillips has tallied 3.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and eight QB hits so far in 2026.
